summary: Opportunistic IMDS probe (from runner box, session-side, or via SSRF). When credentials come back, this is T3 initial-access on the cloud plane. Uniquely, exploit_via_ssrf turns a crawler-confirmed SSRF into real STS credential extraction — that is T4 chain. Every credential finding is a live capture, not a posture claim.

findings.title_pattern: Cloud IMDS reachable from this host
findings.tier_evidence: Link-local IMDS answered ONLY from inside a cloud VPC — deterministic vuln signal (from the runner's context).
findings.promotion_notes: Chain into imds_iam_credentials_exposed / gcp_service_account_token_exposed / azure_managed_identity_token_exposed (module already does when tokens are returned).
findings.tester_next_step: curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/  # from the runner or a session on the host
n/a — informational label used to steer per-provider probes

findings.tier_evidence: GET /latest/meta-data/ answers 200 WITHOUT the X-aws-ec2-metadata-token header — deterministic.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain with imds_iam_credentials_exposed to pull tokens without needing a mint call.

findings.title_pattern: AWS IAM role credentials exposed via IMDS
findings.tier_evidence: recce pulled a full STS AccessKeyId + SecretAccessKey + SessionToken JSON — that IS a live foothold on the AWS control plane. Not proof-of-concept, actual working credential.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-run `aws sts get-caller-identity`, then enumerate role permissions with iam.list_attached_role_policies, then try common escalations (iam:PassRole, secretsmanager:GetSecretValue).
findings.tester_next_step: export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=... AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=... AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=... ; aws sts get-caller-identity ; aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name <role> ; aws s3 ls ; aws secretsmanager list-secrets

findings.tier_evidence: Real regex hits on real user-data text — passwords, AKIAs, private keys, github tokens are extracted verbatim.
findings.promotion_notes: Push extracted AKIAs into aws_probe / secretsmanager loop; feed private keys into ssh_key_store for lateral SSH.
findings.tester_next_step: grep -Eo 'AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|-----BEGIN[^-]+PRIVATE KEY-----' <user-data-dump>  ; then aws sts get-caller-identity with each key

findings.title_pattern: GCP service-account OAuth2 access token exposed via IMDS
findings.tier_evidence: Live OAuth2 access_token; usable directly as Authorization: Bearer against any Google API.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-enum: projects.get, iam.serviceAccounts.list, secretmanager.list; if broad, try cross-project impersonation.

findings.title_pattern: Azure managed identity access token(s) exposed via IMDS
findings.tier_evidence: Live MSI JWTs for multiple audiences (ARM, storage, keyvault, graph).
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-enum: /subscriptions/{sub}/resourceGroups; then keyvault.getSecret and blob container list; MS Graph directory read.

findings.title_pattern: Alibaba Cloud RAM STS credentials exposed via IMDS
findings.tier_evidence: Live temporary RAM STS keys extracted.
findings.promotion_notes: aliyun cli / OSS list; escalate through ram:ListPoliciesForRole.
findings.tester_next_step: export ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID=... ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET=... ALIBABA_CLOUD_SECURITY_TOKEN=... ; aliyun sts GetCallerIdentity

findings.title_pattern: IMDS reachable through host's HTTP proxy (Capital One 2019 pattern)
findings.tier_evidence: The probe SUCCEEDS only if a proxy on the host actively forwards to link-local (via absolute-URI or CONNECT) and IMDS answers — that is a proof-of-concept that any SSRF becomes cloud creds.
findings.promotion_notes: Use proxy to fetch security-credentials/<role> and stash the STS keys.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -x http://<proxy-host>:8080 http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/  # if roles listed, pull the credential JSON via the same proxy

findings.title_pattern: IMDSv2 hop-limit too high (referenced in module doc but not emitted)
findings.tier_evidence: Doc lists this kind but the module code emits no such finding.
findings.promotion_notes: Add: after mint_token, read the response 'X-Aws-Ec2-Metadata-Token-Ttl-Seconds' echo; separately parse the hop-limit from instance metadata options (which requires cred). Not straightforward pre-auth.
findings.tester_next_step: aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids <id> --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].MetadataOptions'  # needs a credential

findings.tier_evidence: Identity document read — recon for accountId/subscriptionId/projectId.

findings.title_pattern: AWS instance SSH public keys disclosed via IMDS
findings.tester_next_step: curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/public-keys/0/openssh-key ; then grep across engagement authorized_keys mines

findings.title_pattern: Web SSRF chained through to IMDS credential extraction
findings.tier_evidence: This is a CHAIN: crawler-confirmed SSRF is replayed through the vulnerable parameter against IMDS, and real STS/OAuth2/MSI credentials come back. exploit_via_ssrf is initiated by crawl.py and lands in this finding — the loop from bug to cloud-plane cred is closed.
findings.promotion_notes: Already a full chain. Add: post-crack usage against ARM/AWS API to prove control.
findings.tester_next_step: Use the captured STS keys immediately: aws sts get-caller-identity ; then map the role's IAM policy and pursue AdministratorAccess / iam:PassRole paths.
